item.title: Notes and Note workspaces
item.description:
Open Notes from the app rail or press Ctrl+Shift+N. On macOS, press Cmd+Shift+N. Notes fills the full window width. Choose Terminal in the Notes header to return to the terminal. Pressing Esc does not close Notes; Esc can still dismiss a Notes dialog or menu.

Ctrl+Shift+M (Cmd+Shift+M on macOS) slides a quick-notes panel in from the right. The terminal stays where it is. Press the same keys, or Esc, to slide it back. Drag the left edge to resize the panel, or focus that edge and press the arrow keys. The width is remembered. The dropdown lists notes in the default Note workspace, and + beside it creates a note. Search matches the title, the filename, the path, and the tags, and shows how many notes remain, such as 2 of 40. This is not a second notes folder. An edit saves about 700ms after you stop typing, the same way the Notes page saves. Unsaved text stays if you switch notes or slide the panel away before that save finishes. Ctrl+Shift+N still opens this page.
